most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei) with pneumonia, septic shock and splenic abscess; main alternatives are Q fever (Coxiella burnetii from bandicoot exposure) and leptospirosis
one_line_reason: A smoker in tropical Far North Queensland who dug soil and handled a dead bandicoot without a mask now has septic shock, bilateral pneumonia, confusion, AKI, thrombocytopenia, liver injury and a splenic lesion. That pattern points to melioidosis, or to a bandicoot zoonosis such as Q fever. Leptospirosis is the best listed match, but it does not explain the splenic lesion.
